items.caption: A modern rendering of 要 in Shuowen seal-script style. The Shuowen account interprets the character as the body's middle and describes a person holding the waist, while analyses of the earlier graph remain disputed.
items.alt: Black seal-script style glyph with a tall central form containing two openings, flanked by curved strokes on both sides.
items.selection_reason: This identified seal-script rendering offers a useful visual reference for 要's historical form; its accompanying historical interpretation is explicitly uncertain, and the cited study reports Shang and Western Zhou examples alongside competing analyses.

limitations.text: This is a modern vector redraw, not an ancient inscription image, and cannot settle the disputed interpretation of the early graph. The cited study lists early inscription examples but does not establish what word each specific inscription records.
